stem: A facility switches water sources. The new source has nearly the same pH as the old source but a higher EC. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The sources are probably equivalent because similar pH usually means their dissolved-ion composition, alkalinity, and buffering behavior will remain comparable in the nutrient program
The higher EC indicates a different dissolved-ion load, so source-water records should be reviewed before assuming the same program will behave identically
The higher EC means irrigation volume should be reduced in the same proportion so the crop receives the same total mineral load
The similar pH shows alkalinity and ion composition are unchanged, so the existing nutrient program can be carried over without verification
rationale: Similar pH does not establish equivalent source-water chemistry. A higher EC indicates a changed ionic load and warrants comparison with prior source-water records before management changes are made.
